announcement BEFORE the ceremony opens. A participant added afterwards
cannot be shown not to have been added because of what the earlier
Every key must be one that was already publicly that person's before this
ceremony. A key minted for the occasion produces a signature anyone could
have made -- worth exactly what no signature is worth, while looking like
more. 'published_at' is where a stranger can see that the key was theirs;
it is not fetched by the verifier, it is for the human reading the roster.
The key material is carried inline rather than as a fingerprint, so
verification never depends on fetching anything: a verifier that has to go
and get a key has made that fetch the weakest thing in the chain.
'independent_of_operator' is the field the whole roster exists for. It is
a claim this tooling cannot check -- only that someone made it and signed.
Set it false for anyone who shares a failure mode with the party deploying
the pool: same company, same machine, same person. An automated agent on
the operator's machine IS the operator.
